reviewer: 96-11 executor, fresh context, wrote none of the lines or the rewrites

rows.note: Meets the round-1 note: it has the attitude now and both halves, the bounce and the lingering cushion.
The dark is scoped to the fight now, which is all the rule delivers.
Lesser foes plus the hedge 'unless they know better' matches the below-your-level resist rule.
'Slightly easier target' is honest for a +1 to hit.
No longer nullifies the blow. 'A bruise where a break would have been' is the upper edge of what half damage on one attack delivers, but it stays a bruise and not a miss.
The cutlery drawer gives it the attitude the plain inventory lacked.
Good: hits harder (moa-damage) and the nightly dents (moa-patch). Bad: neither talk nor walk out (moa-parley, moa-never-leaves). The joke is new and the rules phrase is no longer lifted.

The banned stem is gone from the line. Good: the kit (samurai-kit). Bad: never acts first and never runs (samurai-never). The canon SUB_NOTE rules text still says suicidal; that is the user's decision, not this review's.
The count is gone. It names no limit, but the line is the act of bracing and RULES carries the two-blow limit; it does not contradict it.
Has attitude now. 'A single huge swing' names the one-swing scope, not a rule number; kept.
The glare that extracts a confession is the joke the plain restatement lacked.
Scoped to beasts as the rule is; skeletons are Walking Dead in the bestiary, so the aside is true.
First verdict (added after round 1 by 96-12). Deadpan, number-free, and 'a breather before the encore' matches the wait before a repeat without naming it.
'Hurt already' contradicts the rule, which finishes anything under a fixed 15 hp: a fresh small foe qualifies and a wounded big one may not; say the foe is low or has little left, with no number.
First verdict. 'A short while' is vague, with no unit or count; the image fits a to-hit penalty.
First verdict. 'Thinking about it' is the lost turn, and it is a hit-only effect as in the rule.
First verdict. 'Your whole side' and 'for a moment' match the party-wide, short penalty; no number.
'A few rounds' is a duration in disguise (a unit with a vague count, the cooldown); keep the pep-talk joke and say it needs time or a rest, with no unit.
First verdict. 'For a crowd' is the two-foe minimum and 'nobody gets the full helping' is the half damage, both without a number.
'A few rounds off' is a duration in disguise (a unit with a vague count, the cooldown); keep the eyes-left joke and let the cooldown be a rest or a foe who has caught on, with no unit.
First verdict. Slapstick grit, nothing gory; 'barely see' and 'for a while' match the blind rule without a number.
First verdict. 'Foes swing at scenery' and a flee that works are both in the rule; 'for a spell' is an idiom, not a count.

First verdict. Oblique: it never says the trick is an attack, and 'a soldier's habits' covers the Guard loosely; but it names the three spoilers the rule lists and contradicts nothing, and RULES carries the rest.
Has its own deadpan now and keeps the 'then the magic is spent' half of the rule.
'Rather smug about it' is the attitude the restatement lacked; the ability still owns the fine print.
